## The problem

Our team of twelve has drifted into long lived feature branches that often stay open for two to three weeks. Merges have become dreaded events: integration conflicts pile up, code review happens on giant diffs nobody can meaningfully evaluate, and QA discovers cross-feature bugs only after several branches land in the same week. Last quarter we shipped two hotfixes specifically to undo integration regressions that trunk-based development would have surfaced within a day. The root cause is architectural, not a discipline problem: branches isolate work from each other precisely as long as they isolate it from reality.

## The proposal

I propose we adopt trunk-based development over the next month, with these changes:

- All engineers commit directly to main at least once per day, behind feature flags where work is incomplete.
- We retire long lived feature branches in favor of short lived branches that live under 24 hours.
- CI must run on every commit to main, with a strict "fix it or revert it" rule for breakages.
- We adopt feature flags as the standard mechanism for hiding unfinished work in production code.
- We run a two week pilot with one squad before rolling out team-wide, so we can adjust based on real friction.

This mirrors practices at Google and other high-velocity engineering organizations, and it directly attacks the integration-pain root cause described above rather than treating its symptoms.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: trunk-based development demands mature CI, comprehensive test coverage, and feature-flag discipline we don't fully have today. If our test suite has gaps, committing incomplete work to main more frequently could destabilize it for everyone rather than one branch owner. I take this seriously — it's why the proposal includes a pilot and an explicit CI investment, not just a policy change. We should be honest that if our test coverage doesn't improve in parallel, this transition will hurt before it helps.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
